item.title: Riley Green’s Confessions: His Slow Burn Success, Touring, Politics & Vintage Cars | Billboard Cover
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to our podcast, where we sit down with the biggest names in music. Today, we're talking to country star Riley Green, our cover star. Riley, thanks for joining us.
Riley Green: Thanks for having me.
Host: Riley, you've been on a roll lately, selling out major venues and touring internationally. What's it been like to see your career take off like this?
Riley Green: It's been amazing. We've been able to accomplish some pretty incredible things, from playing big venues to selling them out. And touring internationally has been a surprise in a good way. I believed we could do it, and it's worked out.
Host: That's terrific. You've even sold out the Bridgestone in Nashville, which is no easy feat. What was that like?
Riley Green: It was a big deal. Nashville's a unique place, and to sell out a hard-ticket venue like Bridgestone, you've got to bring in a lot of fans. But I believed we had enough support, and it was a great night.
Host: Now, when you're on tour, what's a typical show day like for you?
Riley Green: It depends on where we are. Sometimes I like to get out and play golf or explore. But one thing I love to do is thrift shopping and antiquing. And I've developed a bit of a hobby – buying old cars on the road.
Host: That's a unique hobby. How many cars have you bought this way?
Riley Green: [laughs] I think I'm up to 18. Not all of them run, but they look cool.
Host: [laughs] Well, we'll have to see if you can get them all running. Thanks for sharing your story with us, Riley.
Riley Green: Thanks for having me.
[Outro music plays]
Host: That's all for today. Thanks for tuning in. We'll have more from our conversation with Riley Green soon.
